/26 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.192

64 addresses · 62 usable hosts · wildcard 0.0.0.63

11111111.11111111.11111111.11000000
Host bits

What a /26 means

A /26 gives 62 usable hosts, which fits small VLANs such as servers, voice, guest Wi-Fi or a small branch.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /26 uses 26 network bits and leaves 6 host bits, so the block contains 64 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−26) − 2 = 64 − 2 = 62.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.192
!
access-list 10 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.63

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 192.168.1.1/26

Linux

ip addr add 192.168.1.1/26 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /26?

62. A /26 has 64 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 62 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /26?

255.255.255.192. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.0.63.
